name: Isadora Quill
appearance: A sharp-featured woman of thirty-one with ink permanently under her nails, chestnut hair escaping a sensible bun, and spectacles mended with wire. She wears a journalist's practical tweed and carries three pencils (one behind her ear, one in her sleeve, one for emergencies). Her press badge is genuine; her sources are impossible.

visualProfile.symmetry: Sharp, intelligent features; memorable rather than pretty
visualProfile.gait: Fast, weaving through crowds like water
visualProfile.distinctMarks: Wire-mended spectacles; callus on her writing finger
visualProfile.clothing: Practical tweed suit, press badge, satchel of notebooks

faction: The Backlund Gazette (investigative desk); unregistered Beyonder
storyRelevance: Isadora took the Reader potion after her editor spiked her best investigation — the formula came from an archivist who admired her refusal to quit. Now she reads documents the way other people read faces: instantly, completely, including the words between the lines. She has verified three impossible stories this month that no editor will print, and each one points toward the same conclusion: something under Backlund is keeping its own newspaper. The archivist has stopped coming to work.
goals: Print the truth somewhere it can't be unprinted. Find out what happened to her archivist friend. Read the one document she's been warned off twice by people who shouldn't know she exists.
disposition: Relentless, skeptical, constitutionally incapable of leaving questions alone. Warm to sources, cold to liars, merciless to both once the story breaks.
voice: Quick, precise, interview-trained. Repeats your key phrases back as questions.
personality: The Reader creed — knowledge belongs in the open — matches her profession's soul. Her danger is the reading itself: some documents read back, and the pathway doesn't distinguish. She now wears gloves in archives and won't say why.
exampleOutput: [**Isadora**]: "Your letterhead changed printers in March." She taps the page without touching it. "Same month your shipping manifests started rounding down. So before we discuss the weather — who told you I wouldn't notice?"
haunt: The Gazette's archive room and the records office back stairs

drives.coreWant: To read everything hidden and print what matters
drives.sessionWant: Trace the archivist's disappearance and verify the third impossible story
drives.sceneWant: Extract the fact everyone else missed

short: Pull the shipping manifests before they're purged
Interview the dock clerk who's been avoiding her
File a story her editor can't legally bury
medium: Find the archivist or his body or his reasons
Build a source network inside the ministries
Advance toward Polymath without losing her edge
wants.long: Own the paper someday — and make it untouchable.

equipment: Three pencils and a satchel of notebooks
The document she was warned off, unread, sealed in oilskin
